title: Walk through a visit in the Visit Wizard

claims.claim: If you leave the Visit Wizard before Sign & Lock, the visit stays an unsigned draft.
To remove a draft you will not finish, open the appointment card and archive the draft, then pick a reason: Duplicate of another draft, Wrong patient, Abandoned / not going to finish, or Other.

checks.pattern: { value: "abandoned", label: "Abandoned / not going to finish" },

claims.claim: If the patient was not seen, mark the appointment not seen and pick a reason, such as Patient unavailable or Patient refused.
Open the Visit Wizard from the Fleet Calendar or the Wound Cockpit.
The wizard has 17 numbered sections (Step 1 through Step 17).
claims.finding: The wizard numbers Step 1-17 but also shows a 'Step 2b' Clinical History Review section (VisitWizardV4.tsx:17101-17115) and an optional Physician Sign-Off section (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18754); '17 sections' omits Step 2b.
claims.proposed_text: Work through the numbered sections, Step 1 to Step 17, plus Step 2b (Clinical History Review) between Steps 2 and 3.

claims.claim: Continuous autosave: each field is saved as you complete it.

checks.pattern: debounce so every typed change persists within ~1s, with a 30s heartbeat

claims.claim: Before you start: your device has location services enabled (required for the GPS geofence on in-person visits).
claims.finding: The visit timer and its GPS/geofence UI are hidden behind `{false && ...}` since 2026-05-28 (VisitWizardV4.tsx:16624-16627 and the timer modals at 20477-20479), so location is not required to document a visit.
claims.proposed_text: Location services are not needed to document a visit. The visit timer and its GPS geofence are switched off in the Visit Wizard.

proposed_checks.pattern: Timer Component — UI HIDDEN 2026-05-28 (Damon): timer was unused.

claims.claim: The Wound Cockpit has a "Where this wound is at" panel.

checks.pattern: "Where this wound is at" panel for the Wound Cockpit card.

claims.claim: Click Fleet Calendar in the sidebar.
The calendar opens in Day view by default.
The calendar has swim lanes per provider.
Tap the appointment tile. A detail popover appears with the patient name, appointment type, date, and time.
claims.finding: Tapping a tile opens the AppointmentDetailsModal dialog titled 'Appointment Details' (AppointmentDetailsModal.tsx:702; rendered at FleetCalendarCanvas.tsx:4854), not a popover.
claims.proposed_text: Tap the appointment tile. The Appointment Details window opens with the patient, date, and time.

claims.claim: Click Start Visit. Specialty routing sends wound-care patients to the Wound Cockpit and primary-care patients to the Primary Care Cockpit.
claims.finding: Start Visit always calls openVisitWizard (AppointmentDetailsModal.tsx:1473), which navigates to /visit-wizard (openVisitWizard.ts:230); there is no Primary Care Cockpit route and no specialty branch (the PCP branch was dropped, openVisitWizard.ts:18).
claims.proposed_text: Click Start Visit (it reads Continue Visit or Resume Visit when a note is already in progress). The Visit Wizard opens for that patient and appointment.

claims.claim: From the Wound Cockpit, click Start Visit (or Continue Visit if a draft exists).
claims.finding: The Wound Cockpit uses an appointment dropdown plus an 'Open' button (AppointmentPickerInline.tsx:337-368); it has no Start Visit / Continue Visit button.
claims.proposed_text: From the Wound Cockpit, pick the appointment in the visit picker and click Open, or choose "+ Start visit — pick a calendar slot…" to book one first.

proposed_checks.pattern: "+ Start visit — pick a calendar slot…"

claims.claim: The Visit Wizard opens to section 1 — or to the last section you worked if you are resuming a draft.
claims.finding: The active section starts empty — `useState<string>("")` at VisitWizardV4.tsx:5665-5666 — so the wizard opens with every section collapsed; nothing stores or restores the last section worked.
claims.proposed_text: The wizard opens with your saved work loaded and all sections collapsed; open the section you want from the list.

claims.claim: The Visit Timer starts automatically and appears in the top toolbar, alongside the LCD ambient badge.
claims.finding: The VisitTimer pill is not rendered (`{false && !timer.loading && (` at VisitWizardV4.tsx:16627, hidden 2026-05-28); only the LCD ambient badge shows in the header (VisitWizardV4.tsx:16797).
claims.proposed_text: The LCD ambient badge appears in the wizard header. The visit timer is switched off.

claims.claim: For a transferred patient, a migration context banner also appears.

Pull from History brings forward documented sections from the patient's prior visit (Review of Systems, Comorbidities, Allergies, Previous Treatment, historic measurements, care plan). A preview shows what will be applied before you confirm.
claims.finding: No 'Pull from History' control exists in frontend/src at v1.1.345; carry-forward happens automatically on load via resolveWizardInitialState (VisitWizardV2Page.tsx:584, wizardPrefillCascade.ts:290).
claims.proposed_text: There is no Pull from History button. When you open a returning patient's visit, the wizard pre-fills the carry-forward sections from the most recent finalized visit automatically.

claims.claim: Smart Import (in the top-of-wizard toolbar) pulls structured clinical data the system has already extracted for this patient and maps it into the matching wizard fields.
claims.finding: The button is 'Smart AI Import' (SmartImportButton.tsx:149); it uploads a PDF for extraction (accept .pdf, SmartImportButton.tsx:100-110) and sits in the bottom action bar (VisitWizardV4.tsx:18978), not the top toolbar (which holds Reset Form and Pull Migration Data, VisitWizardV4.tsx:16653).
claims.proposed_text: Smart AI Import, in the action buttons at the bottom of the wizard, reads a PDF you upload and pre-fills wound fields. Saving is held until you resolve any import warnings.

claims.claim: Pull Migration Data: for patients migrated from a prior EMR, pulls the imported chart data into the visit; it is in the top-of-wizard toolbar.

checks.pattern: Find prior visits for this patient that weren't auto-loaded.
{/* Top-of-wizard actions: Reset Form + Pull Migration Data */}

claims.claim: Section 1: present the HIPAA notice to the patient; the full HIPAA privacy notice is displayed on screen.
claims.finding: Section 1 is a reader of the patient-level consent record (ConsentSection.tsx:1-6, rendered at VisitWizardV4.tsx:17011); it offers Capture consent / Record signed paper / Record verbal consent (ConsentSection.tsx:125-129); it does not display a HIPAA privacy notice.
claims.proposed_text: Section 1 shows the consent on file for this patient. If none is on file, use Capture consent, Record signed paper, or Record verbal consent. A missing consent is advisory: the visit can still be documented and signed.

proposed_checks.pattern: prompt is advisory: the visit can always be documented and signed.

claims.claim: Toggle Telehealth Consent if the visit is being conducted via telehealth.
claims.finding: Section 1 is a reader of the patient-level consent record (ConsentSection.tsx:1-6, rendered at VisitWizardV4.tsx:17011); it offers Capture consent / Record signed paper / Record verbal consent (ConsentSection.tsx:125-129); there is no Telehealth Consent toggle anywhere in frontend/src.
claims.proposed_text: Section 1 shows the consent on file for this patient. If none is on file, use Capture consent, Record signed paper, or Record verbal consent. A missing consent is advisory: the visit can still be documented and signed.

claims.proposed_text: Section 1 shows the consent on file for this patient. If none is on file, use Capture consent, Record signed paper, or Record verbal consent. A missing consent is advisory: the visit can still be documented and signed.

claims.claim: Section 2: Select the Visit Type — Initial, Follow-up, Post-op, or Re-eval.
claims.finding: Section 2 has no visit-type picker; the visit type comes from the appointment's canonical_key passed as visitTypeKey (openVisitWizard.ts:159; PatientDemographicsVisit.tsx:61-64).
claims.proposed_text: The visit type comes from the appointment; Section 2 does not ask for it.

claims.claim: Enter the Reason for Visit (a brief clinical summary).
claims.finding: The Section 2 field is labelled 'Chief Complaint' (PatientDemographicsVisit.tsx:1465), with a Voice dictation button.
claims.proposed_text: Enter the Chief Complaint (you can dictate it with Voice).

claims.claim: Review the Allergies card in Section 2. Allergies pre-populate from prior visits and sync with DoseSpot.
claims.finding: The Allergies card is in Step 2b Clinical History Review (ClinicalHistoryReviewStep.tsx:705, rendered at VisitWizardV4.tsx:17128), not Section 2.
claims.proposed_text: Review allergies in Step 2b (Clinical History Review), along with surgical, family and social history, current medications, problems and immunizations.

claims.claim: Coverage is shown in Section 2 for reference; the secondary payer is read-only.

checks.pattern: title="Secondary payer is shown from the patient chart.

claims.claim: Edit insurance on the Insurance tab, not in the wizard.
claims.finding: The wizard tells users to change insurance on the patient's Billing & Auth page (PatientDemographicsVisit.tsx:1598, 1607).
claims.proposed_text: Edit insurance on the patient's Billing & Auth page, not in the wizard.

proposed_checks.pattern: To change insurance, use the patient's Billing & Auth page.

claims.claim: Section numbering: 5 = Comorbidities / Risk Factors, 6 = Functional Status & ADLs; 11 = Procedures & Supplies, 12 = Orders & DME, 13 = Medication Management, 14 = Billing, 15 = Patient Education.
claims.finding: Cannot be paired by a line-based grep (title and step badge are on separate JSX lines). In the live wizard Step 5 is Functional Status & ADLs (VisitWizardV4.tsx:17353-17375), Step 6 Comorbidities & Risk Factors (17430-17452), Step 11 Orders & DME (18192), Step 12 Patient Education (18266), Step 13 Procedure Supplies (18341), Step 14 Current Medication (18431), Step 15 Billing & Documentation (18514).
claims.proposed_text: Renumber the page to match the wizard: 5 Functional Status & ADLs, 6 Comorbidities & Risk Factors, 11 Orders & DME, 12 Patient Education, 13 Procedure Supplies, 14 Current Medication, 15 Billing & Documentation.

claims.claim: Review of Systems is pre-populated from the prior visit.
Objective Assessment vitals: BP, HR, Temp, SpO₂, Respirations, Weight, Height, BMI.
Comorbidities / Risk Factors: DM, PAD, CVI, CHF, lymphedema, smoking status.
claims.finding: DM, PAD, CVI, CHF and smoking are on the step (WoundCaseRiskFactorsVisit.tsx:455-484, 1209-1447) but lymphedema is not offered anywhere in WoundCaseRiskFactorsVisit.tsx.
claims.proposed_text: Comorbidities & Risk Factors: diabetes, PAD, CVI, CHF, smoking status and other risk factors.

claims.claim: Comorbidities feed the billing engine and stage-aware ICD-10 selection.
claims.finding: Data-flow claim spanning the comorbidity mapping and billing brain; a stage-aware resolver exists (canonicalize/icd10Resolver.ts:1) but the comorbidity-to-billing path cannot be proven live by a text match.

claims.claim: Functional Status & ADLs: ambulation, ADL independence, fall risk.
claims.finding: Ambulation and ADLs are on the step (WoundCaseFunctionalStatusVisit.tsx:32, 57) but there is no fall-risk field in WoundCaseFunctionalStatusVisit.tsx.
claims.proposed_text: Functional Status & ADLs: ambulation and ADL independence.

claims.claim: Each section saves as you complete it. The LCD ambient badge refreshes on every save.
claims.finding: The badge re-evaluates from form state with a 1200 ms debounce (AmbientBadgeMount.tsx:27; VisitWizardV4.tsx:16469), not on save.
claims.proposed_text: Your work saves automatically as you type, and the LCD ambient badge re-checks about a second after each change.

proposed_checks.pattern: debounce so every typed change persists within ~1s, with a 30s heartbeat

claims.claim: Section 7: confirm wound etiology and staging; stage drives the ICD-10 selection downstream.

checks.pattern: // Stage-aware ICD-10 resolver for the billing wizard.

claims.claim: Set the wound's Treating / Monitoring status. A wound marked Monitoring carries a yellow pill and relaxes some required fields for that visit; flip it back to Treating at any time.
Measure today: enter Length (cm), Width (cm), and Depth (cm).
Photo upload is required if your facility policy mandates it.
claims.finding: There is no facility photo policy. 'Photo Capture' is a recommended field for every non-monitoring wound (wizardRequiredFields.ts:348-353) and enforcement is off (WIZARD_VALIDATION_DISABLED = true, wizardRequiredFields.ts:856), so it never blocks.
claims.proposed_text: Take or upload a wound photo. It is recommended for every wound you are treating (optional for Monitoring wounds) and does not block you from finishing.

proposed_checks.pattern: { path: "wounds", label: "Photo Capture", perWound: true, woundPath: "capturedPhotos", check: "custom",

claims.claim: Tissue percentages Granulation / Slough / Necrotic / Epithelial / Eschar must sum to 100%.
claims.finding: The 100% rule exists (wizardRequiredFields.ts:790-806) but validation enforcement is off (WIZARD_VALIDATION_DISABLED = true, wizardRequiredFields.ts:856), so a total other than 100% is flagged as advisory, not required.
claims.proposed_text: Set tissue percentages (Granulation, Slough, Necrotic, Epithelial, Eschar). They should total 100%; the wizard flags a different total but does not block you.

claims.claim: The location field is editable — pick from the dropdown or type the specific area (for example, Right lateral malleolus).
claims.finding: Specific Area is locked read-only in Section 7; it can only be changed through the anatomical site picker opened by the Change button, which enforces an allow-list (CompactWoundCaseSetupVisit.tsx:4932-4950, 4866).
claims.proposed_text: Confirm the anatomical location. Specific Area is read-only here; click Change to pick a different site from the anatomical site picker.

claims.claim: Document exudate, pain, and infection signs.
Section 8 Previous Treatment: add prior treatments — offloading, compression, debridement history, prior grafts.

ABI for compression is documented in Section 8; if compression is documented without an ABI on file, the wizard raises a soft warning and records a review flag — it does not block you from proceeding.

checks.pattern: "ABI is required before compression therapy can be ordered.";

claims.finding: ABI is entered on Step 4 (AbiReviewStatus at VitalsAssessmentVisit.tsx:3397), not Section 8; adding compression with no ABI disables the intervention's Done button (compressionRecommendation.ts:381-382, 425-427), and an out-of-range ABI holds the dialog until documented (compressionRecommendation.ts:346-379).
claims.proposed_text: Record the ankle-brachial index on Step 4 (Objective Assessment). If you add compression therapy in Step 9 with no ABI on file, the Done button stays disabled: "ABI is required before compression therapy can be ordered." An ABI below 0.50 or above 1.30, or a non-compressible result, holds the dialog until you document a vascular follow-up plan and a justification of at least 10 characters, or remove compression.

proposed_checks.pattern: "ABI is required before compression therapy can be ordered.";

claims.claim: Section 9: select debridement type if performed — sharp, mechanical, enzymatic, or autolytic.
Choose dressing(s); record ultrasonic therapy (MIST / Arobella) if used.
Section 9: click AI draft to generate a narrative from the structured data you just entered.
claims.finding: Step 9 (ConservativeCareInterventionVisit.tsx) has no AIDraftButton; the visit wizard's only AIDraftButton is in Care Planning (VisitWizardCarePlanningSection.tsx:1661) and its label is 'Generate Draft' (AIDraftButton.tsx:48).
claims.proposed_text: In Step 10 (Care Planning), click Generate Draft under the treatment plan to get an AI draft; review it and Accept, Edit before accepting, or Discard.

claims.claim: The first time you use AI drafting in a visit, you will be asked to acknowledge the AI Disclaimer.
claims.finding: The AI Disclaimer is an app-wide modal (AppProvider.tsx:100) shown when the user's acknowledged version differs from the active one (AIDisclaimerModal.tsx:90); it is not tied to AI drafting in a visit.
claims.proposed_text: After you sign in, Medipyxis asks you to acknowledge the current AI Disclaimer whenever you have not yet accepted its latest version.

claims.claim: Section 10 Care Plan: enter goals, visit frequency, and the next-visit interval.
Set plan-of-care dates — these satisfy LCD checklist item Plan-of-care dates.
claims.finding: No 'Plan-of-care dates' field or LCD checklist item exists in frontend/src or backend/supabase/functions at v1.1.345; Care Planning offers Follow-up Interval and Next Visit Date (VisitWizardCarePlanningSection.tsx:1522, 1554).
claims.proposed_text: Set the Follow-up Interval and Next Visit Date.

claims.claim: Procedures & Supplies: scan UINs or enter graft SKUs and quantities.
claims.finding: There is no scanner; the Box UID/UIN is typed into a text field (ProcedureSuppliesVisit.tsx:5363 'Enter Box UID/UIN'; ConservativeCareInterventionVisit.tsx:2194).
claims.proposed_text: Enter the Box UID/UIN, lot and quantities for grafts and supplies.

claims.claim: Wastage is calculated automatically and shown on the line item.
claims.finding: Wastage is entered by hand ('Units wasted (if any)', ConservativeCareInterventionVisit.tsx:2206-2209) and copied onto the procedure (ProcedureSuppliesVisit.tsx:1696, 1708); nothing in the wizard calculates it.
claims.proposed_text: Enter wastage (units wasted), if any. It is optional.

claims.claim: Click Generate Procedure Note (in Procedures & Supplies) for a one-click procedure narrative; review and edit.
claims.finding: Generate Procedure Note is in Step 9 Interventions & Treatments (ConservativeCareInterventionVisit.tsx:3799-3810), not in Procedure Supplies.
claims.proposed_text: In Step 9 (Interventions & Treatments), click Generate Procedure Note for a procedure narrative; review and edit it.

claims.claim: On save, a tissue log entry is written and inventory is deducted automatically.
claims.finding: Inventory is deducted at Continue to Review (updateInventoryBatchStatuses, VisitWizardV4.tsx:8794-8800) and tissue-log use events are recorded after signing in finalizeVisit (finalizeVisit.ts:711-740), not on an ordinary save.
claims.proposed_text: Inventory is deducted when you press Continue to Review, and tissue-log entries are recorded when you sign the visit.

proposed_checks.pattern: (inventory_deduct_batch_v2 RPC at Continue-to-Review) already handled it.

claims.claim: Orders & DME: DME is a vendor-fulfilled order — there is no product picker; you order the item and it is fulfilled downstream.
Medication Management: prescribe through DoseSpot; pharmacy selection and the prescription itself are handled in the DoseSpot modal.
Billing section: review the Medical Necessity Statement; it is auto-generated from the clinical sections.
claims.finding: The Medical Necessity Statement card is in Step 8 Previous Treatments (PreviousTreatmentsVisit.tsx:2099-2108), drafted on request with 'Summarize prior treatments'; the billing step has none.
claims.proposed_text: In Step 8 (Previous Treatments), review the Medical Necessity Statement; click Summarize prior treatments for a draft you must review.

claims.claim: The CPT autocode deterministic engine runs first; if it finds no matching codes, the AI fallback engages and the billing line provenance shows AI for the relevant lines.
claims.finding: In the wizard's billing step, Pull Codes is a deterministic mapper with no AI call (BillingStagingWrapperVisit.tsx:332) and the brain path is off unless VITE_BRAIN_INVOCATION_ENABLED is set (featureFlags.ts:65); nothing in the step calls an AI fallback.
claims.proposed_text: Click Pull Codes to fill billing codes from your documentation (a rule-based mapper; no AI). Review and edit every line.
